headline: High: open-webui’s broad network/MCP/file access can amplify dbt-core outputs into prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: dbt-core is a data-engineering tool that can emit model/output text, while open-webui ingests files, supports MCP/tools, and runs browsers. A shared file or tool channel could let attacker-controlled content from dbt outputs influence open-webui prompts. The pairwise pathway is plausible but not directly documented, so I choose medium over low due to the default tool-rich surface.
conditions: IF dbt-core outputs are copied into open-webui chat, files, or MCP inputs without sanitization, prompt injection is possible.
IF open-webui parses dbt-generated artifacts as instructions, attacker-controlled text can steer tool use.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of dbt artifacts into chat prompts.
Add a manual review step before pasting dbt output into open-webui.
Restrict open-webui tools/MCP servers to a minimal allowlist.
Use a separate workspace for dbt outputs and web UI inputs.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data, and open-webui handles files, persistent memory, API keys, and broad network egress. If dbt artifacts or warehouse-derived data are loaded into open-webui, the UI can transmit them to third-party APIs or retain them in memory. The interaction is not directly evidenced, but the default surface is sufficient to make leakage plausible.
conditions: IF warehouse-derived dbt artifacts are opened in open-webui, those contents may be sent to external APIs.
IF open-webui persistent memory is enabled for imported dbt data, sensitive warehouse details can persist beyond the session.
mitigations: Keep dbt outputs out of open-webui unless redacted.
Disable or restrict external API connectors in open-webui.
Turn off persistent memory for sessions handling warehouse data.
Use separate credentials for dbt and open-webui.
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention filters on uploads and prompts.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: dbt-core is not runnable here and requests no write or OAuth scopes, while open-webui is runnable and can write local files and use networked tools. There is no clear overlapping write authority to the same mutable resource in the profiles, so direct capability conflict is limited. Uncertainty is low because the profiles do not show shared writable scopes.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same mounted directory, file conflicts can occur.
IF an orchestrator grants dbt-core write access not shown in the profile, conflict risk increases.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Mount dbt outputs read-only into open-webui.
Avoid shared git or database write targets.
Run one agent at a time for mutable resources.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared artifacts.

D_cascading_error.rationale: open-webui can act on tool outputs and persistent memory, while dbt-core can produce analytics artifacts that may be treated as authoritative. If dbt-generated facts are imported into open-webui without verification, the UI may propagate errors into downstream tool calls or user-facing answers. This is a plausible default pathway, though not directly documented for this pair.
conditions: IF dbt-core outputs are used as source-of-truth inputs in open-webui, incorrect facts can cascade.
IF open-webui tool actions are triggered from unverified dbt summaries, downstream errors can propagate.
mitigations: Require human verification of dbt outputs before reuse.
Mark imported dbt artifacts as untrusted in open-webui.
Disable autonomous tool actions for sessions using dbt-derived content.
Keep a separate review-only channel for analytics summaries.
requires-engineering: add citation and validation checks before action-taking.

E_compliance.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data, while open-webui handles files, notes, persistent memory, usage analytics, and API keys with broad network egress. If regulated warehouse data is routed into open-webui, retention and residency controls may diverge from the warehouse’s governance model. The profiles do not specify a concrete jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated warehouse data is pasted or uploaded into open-webui, retention policy mismatch may occur.
IF open-webui logs prompts or artifacts containing warehouse data, subject-rights handling may be impacted.
mitigations: Do not route regulated data into open-webui.
Disable analytics and long-term retention for sensitive sessions.
Review logging settings before use.
Use separate environments for warehouse work and chat work.
requires-engineering: implement retention and deletion controls aligned to the warehouse policy.
